title: Sticker a two-layer lumber stack with the stickers over the bearers
instruction: Lay two of the pale boards across the two fixed bearers with a gap of about 6 cm between them, lay a dark sticker across those boards directly over each bearer, then lay the other two boards on the stickers, each right above one of the first two.
context: Stacking lumber to air-dry in sawmills, lumber yards and woodworking shops (wood sawing machine operators and hand material movers, O*NET 51-7041 and 53-7062). Boards are laid across bearers in layers with gaps between them, and thin strips called stickers separate the layers so air can flow through the stack. Each sticker must sit directly above a bearer, in a vertical line with the stickers below it, so the weight goes straight down to the bearer (USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Air Drying of Lumber, FPL-GTR-117); a sticker off its bearer leaves the boards over it bending between supports, and they dry bowed. Hand-built stacks are often worked from both sides: each worker brings the pieces on their side while the other places theirs.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three kinds of piece, all plain rectangular blocks. (1) Two bearers: weathered, silver-grey timber battens, 20 mm wide (along x), 320 mm long (along y) and 20 mm tall, fixed to the table, centred at x 20.0 cm and x 36.0 cm, y 0 (each spans y -16 to +16 cm). (2) Four boards: loose red-cedar boards (red-brown), 240 mm long, 40 mm wide and 16 mm thick, 60 g each, lying flat on the table with their long side along x, centred at x 28.0 cm and at y +38.0, +46.0, -38.0 and -46.0 cm: two on each arm's side, 40 mm apart edge to edge. (3) Two stickers: loose near-black stained poplar strips, 280 mm long, 20 mm wide and 16 mm thick, 40 g each, lying flat on the table with their long side along x, centred at x 38.0 cm, y +54.0 cm and y -54.0 cm, outboard of each side's boards. Nothing else is on the table. In the finished stack the boards still lie along x and the stickers along y, across them.
scoring: End state: the score is read from where the pieces lie at the last step. Each board and sticker has two identical broad faces: its 'tilt' is the angle between the vertical and the axis through its broad faces (either face may be down), and its heading is the direction of its long side seen from above (either way round). A piece 'rests on' a support when, seen from above, its underside overlaps the support's top over at least half the area of a square crossing of their two widths (400 square mm for every pair here), and at the centre of that overlap its underside is within 3 mm of the support's top, above or below. A board is laid when it is tilted less than 5 degrees with its long side within 5 degrees of x; a sticker, tilted less than 5 degrees with its long side within 5 degrees of y. Layer 1 is correct when exactly two boards lie laid and resting on both bearers, with a gap between them (the distance between their centres across y, minus 40 mm) of 30 to 90 mm. A sticker is placed when it lies laid and resting on both layer-1 boards; its offset is the distance along x from its centre to the nearer bearer's centre line, and the two stickers must be over different bearers. Layer 2 is the other two boards, each laid and resting on both placed stickers, paired one to one with the layer-1 boards; a top board's offset is the distance across y between its centre and its layer-1 board's centre. Score 0 if any board or sticker ends off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top) or standing on an edge or end (tilted more than 45 degrees). Otherwise: 1.0 if layer 1 is correct, both stickers are placed with offsets of 10 mm or less, and both top boards form layer 2 with offsets of 15 mm or less; 0.75 if layer 1 is correct, both stickers are placed with offsets up to 25 mm and both top boards form layer 2 with offsets up to 30 mm, but not all within the 1.0 limits; 0.5 if layer 1 is correct and both stickers are placed within 10 mm, but layer 2 is not complete within 30 mm (top boards missing, held above the stickers, turned, resting on one sticker, or further off); 0.25 if layer 1 is correct and nothing more counts (stickers missing, both over one bearer, turned, more than 25 mm off, or 10 to 25 mm off without a complete layer 2); 0 in every other case (no correct layer 1: one board on the bearers, three or four, two touching or too far apart, a board turned across them, the stickers laid straight on the bearers). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with every board and sticker still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, the offsets and the gap are read from a top photo against centre-line marks on the bearers' ends and a ruler, and resting from a side photo.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The bearers are fixed to the table; the boards and stickers are plain boxes of uniform density with the stated sizes and masses (no warp, knots or rough-sawn faces). Drying, and the bowing a misplaced sticker causes, are not simulated: the rule is scored from where the stickers lie over the bearers. The scorer sees only the pieces, not the grippers, so a piece held still within 3 mm of its support counts as resting on it.
reset_notes: Put the four boards back flat on their marks with their long side along x, centred at x 28.0 cm and y +38.0, +46.0, -38.0 and -46.0 cm, and the two stickers back flat along x, centred at x 38.0 cm, y +54.0 and -54.0 cm. The bearers stay where they are. Nothing is consumed.
